clips.text_zh: 沙地條油管比人炸咗，東向西邊嗰條。原本可以唔經霍爾木茲海峽出貨，依家冇得揀。衛星圖見到幾個位燒緊，泵站都中招。AI 估要 6 至 12 個月先整返好。沙地佔全球產油 10%，但油價今日反而跌咗。wtf 點解跌嘅。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Big news: oil may hit 150 dollars soon. The Saudi east-west pipeline got hit. Now Saudi oil cannot go around the Strait of Hormuz. It is the only pipeline from the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea. Satellite pictures show fires in several places, and rumors say a pump station was hit too. One AI estimate says repairs will take 6 to 12 months.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ post on Saudi pipeline damage and oil price implications

signal.rationale: Pipeline outage implies supply risk; OP notes ironic dump, contrarian long gold/oil bet

clips.text_en_b2: The east-west pipeline running across Saudi Arabia has reportedly been struck, putting the only land route from the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea out of action. Because tankers now have no choice but to brave the Strait of Hormuz, one would expect prices to spike. Satellite images, however, show fires burning at multiple points, with a pump station apparently caught in the blast as well. Repairs, according to one AI estimate, could drag on for anything between six and twelve months.
clips.text_en_c1: Markets are pricing in a possible oil surge toward 150 dollars following an attack on Saudi Arabia's east-west pipeline, the sole overland route bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. Satellite imagery confirms multiple active fires along the corridor, with unverified reports suggesting at least one pump station sustained damage. Preliminary AI-driven assessments indicate repair timelines ranging from six to twelve months, a window during which exports from the kingdom, accounting for roughly ten percent of global supply, will be severely constrained. Yet, paradoxically, crude futures declined today, a counterintuitive move that has analysts scrambling to identify the underlying catalyst behind the sell-off.
clips.text_en_c2: A critical piece of Saudi energy infrastructure has reportedly been struck: the East-West pipeline, the sole conduit that ferries crude from the Eastern Province across the peninsula to terminals on the Red Sea, thereby bypassing the chokepoint of the Strait of Hormuz. Commercial satellite imagery corroborates multiple burn scars along the corridor, and unverified dispatches indicate that at least one pumping station has likewise been compromised. One machine-learning model — trained on analogous incidents — projects a remediation horizon of somewhere between six and twelve months. Saudi Arabia supplies roughly ten percent of global output. Curiously, oil futures dumped today.

clips.text_en_b2: Tesla and Musk continue to dominate the EV and AI robotics space, with Optimus progress and FSD upgrades keeping the stock ticking along. A single Musk tweet can still send shockwaves through the entire sector, while delivery numbers and the upcoming earnings call have /biz/ traders weighing whether to reload longs or fade the pump. clips.text_en_c1: Tesla, under Musk's stewardship, remains the focal point for anyone tracking the convergence of EVs and AI-driven robotics. Anticipated milestones around Optimus production and further FSD refinements continue to anchor long-term sentiment across the sector. As history has repeatedly demonstrated, a single Musk post on X can reverberate through trading desks worldwide, triggering violent repricings across the EV complex. The current /biz/ thread is dominated by participants dissecting delivery figures and positioning ahead of the next earnings catalyst, debating whether the prevailing setup favours reload longs or fading whatever momentum inevitably emerges.
clips.text_en_c2: Tesla, under Elon's idiosyncratic stewardship, remains the lodestar for anyone positioned in either the EV or the humanoid-robotics complex. The cadence of Optimus disclosures and Full Self-Driving software updates continues to dictate tape action across the broader sector, with a single X post — sometimes nothing more than an emoji-laden provocation — capable of repricing billions in market capitalisation within minutes. Today, the /biz/ thread has devolved into its customary theatre: seasoned traders parsing delivery tallies, anticipating the imminent earnings call, and debating whether to reload their longs or fade the present pump before the next leg resolves.

clips.text_zh: 今日睇返GI report，斜坡穩定性要重新計過factor of safety。土釘長度同間距要check番，地表排水都係重點。Tommy問我beam column check完未，ok 又要OT。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: On site today, going through the GI report again. The slope factor of safety has to be recalculated after the new borehole data came in. Soil nail layout needs a check on length and spacing, and surface drainage is still the weak point. Boss Tommy also asked whether the beam-column check is finished. Another late night at the desk.
clips.source_hint: Repurposed /biz/ URL used as a placeholder slot for civil engineering site reflection
clips.text_en_b2: Back on site today going through the GI report once more, because the latest borehole data has forced a full recalculation of the slope factor of safety. The soil nail layout needs a thorough check on both length and spacing, and surface drainage remains the obvious weak point in the whole setup. On top of that, Tommy wants to know whether the beam-column check is finished. At this rate, another late night at the desk is pretty much written in the stars.
clips.text_en_c1: Back on site today, working through the geotechnical interpretation of the latest GI report. The revised borehole data has invalidated several prior assumptions, necessitating a full recalculation of the slope's factor of safety. Particular attention must be paid to verifying soil nail lengths and spacings against the updated ground model, while surface drainage provisions remain the persistent weak link in the overall scheme. Meanwhile, Tommy has followed up once more regarding the beam-column check, which remains unfinished, and once again overtime beckons.
clips.text_en_c2: Back on site today, poring over the geotechnical interpretive report yet again. The slope's factor of safety must be recomputed in light of the borehole data that arrived late yesterday, and the soil-nail arrangement — its length, its spacing, the integrity of each headed stud — warrants a meticulous cross-check. Surface drainage, predictably, remains the system's perennial weak link, and the grading around the crest has been flagged for remedial profiling. Meanwhile, Tommy has pinged to enquire whether the beam-column design is finally signed off. Another evening spent at the desk, then.

clips.text_zh: 返到屋企繼續睇 RC 設計。load path 由 slab → column → footing，要畫清楚先交到俾 Sum Ho。何生話星期五要傾，我個FE 都未溫完。廢柴。👍
clips.text_en_b1: Working through the reinforced concrete load path tonight: slab transfers load to the beams, beams go down the columns, columns land on the footings, and the footings spread it to the soil. Every joint needs a check, and the detailing decides whether the method actually works on site. Sum Ho wants a meeting on Friday and the FE study notes are still half done.
clips.source_hint: Repurposed /biz/ URL used as placeholder slot for structural engineering study
clips.text_en_b2: Working through the reinforced concrete load path tonight, since every joint needs to be checked before the drawings can go anywhere near Sum Ho. The logic runs cleanly from slab to beam, beam to column, column to footing, and footing to soil, although the detailing is ultimately what decides whether the whole method actually holds up on site. Sum Ho is pushing for a meeting on Friday, while my FE study notes remain stubbornly half done. The hours are piling up fast.
clips.text_en_c1: Spent the evening meticulously tracing the reinforced concrete load path from first principles: slab elements transfer imposed loads to the supporting beams, which in turn channel forces down through the columns and ultimately into the footings before being dispersed into the underlying soil strata. Each connection demands rigorous verification, given that the adequacy of the analytical method ultimately hinges on whether the reinforcement detailing can be executed faithfully on site. Sum Ho has pencilled in a Friday meeting to review progress, yet my FE study materials remain woefully incomplete.
clips.text_en_c2: Settled in at home this evening, methodically tracing the reinforced-concrete load path from first principles: the slab funnels its tributary loading into the beams, which in turn transfer it down through the columns, ultimately depositing it onto isolated pad footings that disperse it into the founding strata. Each node demands careful scrutiny, and the reinforcement detailing — lap lengths, anchorage zones, confinement reinforcement — ultimately determines whether the analytical model translates into constructible reality on the site. Sum Ho has pencilled in a Friday meeting, the FE revision notes remain stubbornly incomplete, and sleep, predictably, is forfeit.

clips.text_zh: /g/ 啱啱有人話 AI model 已經停滯，VC 班友fake news 自己呃自己。睇到我更驚，civil佬遲早俾AI搞埋，靠AI續命。wtf。🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Some posters on /g/ are saying AI companies are fear mongering about their own capabilities so the US government shuts them down and they do not have to pay their debts. The claim is that AI models have hit a wall and each new release shows zero real improvement. If that is true, the whole AI bubble narrative for 2026 is built on hot air.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread claiming AI progress has plateaued
clips.text_en_b2: A growing chorus on /g/ is claiming that AI companies are essentially fear mongering about their own capabilities, presumably so regulators step in and they can wriggle out of their debts. The argument runs that models have hit a wall and every new release shows zero meaningful improvement over the last one. If there is any truth to it, the entire AI bubble narrative for 2026 is built on little more than hot air. As a civvie, that prospect is genuinely terrifying.
clips.text_en_c1: A provocative thread on /g/ contends that the major AI laboratories are engaged in deliberate fearmongering, exaggerating existential risks in order to provoke regulatory intervention that would, conveniently, absolve them of mounting financial obligations. The underlying premise is that frontier models have stagnated: each successive release purportedly demonstrates negligible genuine capability gains over its predecessor. Should this assessment hold any water, the prevailing 2026 narrative of an inexorable AI-driven productivity revolution would rest on remarkably fragile foundations, and those of us whose careers depend on the technology's continued momentum would do well to take notice.
clips.text_en_c2: A provocative thesis has resurfaced on /g/: that the major AI laboratories are, in effect, fear-mongering over their own ostensibly runaway capabilities — calculatedly goading regulators into curtailing them, thereby furnishing a convenient pretext to default on the staggering capital commitments they have accrued. The corollary, naturally, is that frontier model development has stalled irretrievably, and that each successive release — despite the breathless marketing — exhibits negligible empirical gain over its predecessor. If the conjecture holds even partially, the entire 2026 AI-as-GDP-pillar narrative dissolves into little more than vapour and venture-funded wishful thinking.

clips.text_zh: /biz/ 嗰個condo男同我好似。22歲贏錢買樓，依家27做返奴隸。我30，香港condo細到爆，美國先有space。又係學費。lol。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Stuck with a condo he cannot escape. In 2021 when he was 22, he made a bunch of random crypto money from dogecoin. He lived two years with no job, perma vacation, dropped out of school, and bought a condo for 230K dollars. The money ran out. He went back to school, graduated, and now makes 100K a year living in the same condo.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ OP on early crypto gains turned condo prison
clips.text_en_b2: The condo story on /biz/ hits uncomfortably close to home. Back in 2021, when he was 22, he stacked up random crypto profits from dogecoin, blew two years on a perma vacation with no job, dropped out of school, and somehow pulled off a 230K condo purchase. The money dried up, he crawled back to finish his degree, and now at 27 he earns 100K a year while still living in the same unit.
clips.text_en_c1: The condo saga resonating across /biz/ echoes my own circumstances uncomfortably closely. Back in 2021, aged 22, he struck it rich on speculative crypto plays, riding the dogecoin wave into seven-figure territory. Two years of unbridled leisure followed: no employment, perpetual travel, abandoned studies, and ultimately a 230K condominium purchase that felt almost consequence-free at the time. The inevitable reckoning arrived, capital depleted, forcing a return to academia and eventual graduation into a six-figure salary that nonetheless fails to cover the crushing weight of student loans and revolving credit obligations.
clips.text_en_c2: The /biz/ poster's predicament is uncomfortably proximate to my own: at twenty-two, he parlayed a speculative Dogecoin windfall into a condo purchase, squandered two subsequent years in a state of perma-vacation and academic dropout, and now, at twenty-seven, sits marooned in the very asset that once symbolised his liberation. He has graduated, ekes out a hundred grand annually, and yet remains shackled to the same walls, servicing both student loans and accumulated credit-card balances — trapped in what he eloquently terms an inescapable cycle of work, consume, repeat. At thirty, ensconced in a Hong Kong flat of derisory square footage, I empathise entirely.

clips.text_en_b1: Question from /fit/: how do you know when you have bulked enough to cut and escape skinnyfat. In May 2025 he was 83kg and fat with almost no muscle. He cut aggressively until mid April 2026 and got down to 65kg skinnyfat, struggling to bench even the 20kg bar. Then he lean bulked up to now, back at 80kg.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread on transitioning from lean bulk to cut
clips.text_en_b2: A /fit/ user is wondering how to tell when he has bulked enough to cut his way out of skinnyfat territory. In May 2025 he tipped the scales at a flabby 83kg with almost no muscle underneath, then cut hard until mid April 2026 and bottomed out at a stringy 65kg, barely able to bench the 20kg bar. He has since lean bulked back up to 80kg, and his numbers now read 3x8 at one plate on flat bench, 3x6 squat at 90kg, and 3x8…
clips.text_en_c1: A /fit/ regular poses the perennial dilemma: how does one determine when a lean bulk has yielded sufficient muscular development to justify a cutting phase? His trajectory is instructive. In May 2025, he tipped the scales at 83kg, carrying considerable adiposity with negligible muscle mass. An aggressive caloric deficit saw him shed weight steadily until mid-April 2026, bottoming out at a gaunt 65kg, still skinnyfat and barely capable of pressing the unweighted 20kg barbell. A subsequent lean bulk restored him to 80kg, with measurable strength gains: flat bench at one plate for three sets of eight, squats at 90kg for six reps, and deadlifts reaching 120kg.
clips.text_en_c2: A /fit/ regular has documented his physique odyssey with admirable granularity: in May 2025 he tipped the scales at eighty-three kilograms — adipose, untrained, and visually unremarkable. An aggressive cut carried him down to a skeletal sixty-five by April 2026, whereupon he commenced a measured lean bulk, arriving at his present eighty kilograms with markedly improved composition. His working lifts have progressed commensurately — a flat bench of three by eight at one plate, a squat of three by six at ninety kilograms, and a conventional deadlift of three by eight at one-hundred-twenty — though he remains uncertain whether to commence another cut or to capitalise further on his momentum.

clips.text_en_b2: Just wrapped up the Ghost in the Shell anime, and it turned out to be genuinely great. The first couple of episodes felt a bit flat, although once the plot found its footing it kept getting better with every installment. The original poster is now asking the obvious question about when season 2 might drop, while the rest of the /a/ thread is full of fans geeking out over the 90s cyberpunk atmosphere and the philosophical backbone of Section 9.
clips.text_en_c1: Having finally completed the Ghost in the Shell anime, I can attest that its reputation is thoroughly deserved. The opening episodes initially struck me as somewhat uneven, yet the narrative progressively coalesced into something genuinely compelling, with each instalment building upon its predecessor's philosophical and aesthetic foundations. The original poster has since pivoted to inquiring about season 2's prospective release window, while the broader /a/ thread is saturated with enthusiasts extolling the production's quintessential nineties cyberpunk sensibility and the enduring thematic richness surrounding Section 9's operational mandate. Sum Ho had previously championed this title, and his recommendation has proven vindicated.
clips.text_en_c2: Having just concluded the original Ghost in the Shell, I find myself compelled to revise my initial scepticism: the opening instalments felt somewhat sluggish — perhaps weighed down by the conventions of mid-nineties OVA pacing — yet as the narrative progressed through the Laughing Man arc and beyond, the philosophical density, coupled with Production I.G.'s peerless cyberpunk mise-en-scène, became genuinely intoxicating. Section 9's meditations on consciousness, sovereignty, and the fragility of identity remain startlingly prescient. The /a/ thread, predictably, is in raptures, though Sum Ho has been patiently nudging me towards a rewatch for months. Gundam 00, regrettably, remains unwatched.
